_what_this_is: Authored. The Movement Register, brought into the project on 12 September 2026 from the published artifact's live database - Aaron's own saved markup, not the seed. Until this file existed, every movement's VERB and ADJECTIVE lived only on a web page outside the repository, and those are the attributes rounds 1-3 rule on most. The POSITION column is politics ruling 41's re-map; if this file and politics-ideation.md ever disagree, the ruling wins and this file is the bug. Everything else - growth cap, ideology, counties, goals - is read from data/parties.json at run time and is NOT duplicated here.
_sources: Movement Register artifact d5a0bcf2-9e45-42aa-99c2-43f78dfe5204, collection 'movements', 32 documents read 12 September 2026.
The re-map: docs/design/politics-ideation.md line 2296, 'The re-map - 26 live movements placed on the ten positions'.
Ruling 41's cap changes: docs/design/politics-ideation.md line 2386. SPECIFIED AND NOT APPLIED - data/parties.json still reads 0.35 for all three.
The six struck: secession ruling 45, docs/design/secession-ideation.md line 1384.

movements.name: A Free Texas
movements.position_note: RULED by Aaron, 11 September: "I like a Free Texas being fascist because that could be a part of the story that it was taken over by a fascist bloc." The placement is a piece of story, not a translation.
movements.where: Texas entire, plus the Llano Estacado counties of eastern New Mexico
movements.goal: reunite Texas; one Texan state again
movements.aaron_note: I think this is one where it would want the government to reunify at any cost the state of Texas.

movements.name: Acadiana
movements.where: The twenty-two French parishes of Louisiana and the bayou
movements.goal: French in the schools; coastal restoration
movements.aaron_note: I like this one especially as it could become a part of the Gulf Compact and the Gulf Compact could be a unified state? We can talk about that later in governments and diplomacy.

movements.name: Alaskan Independence
movements.position_note: Independence plus resource royalties is libertarian; Anarcho-Capitalism is the alternative.
movements.where: Alaska entire
movements.aaron_note: Looks good.

movements.name: Blue-Collar Populist
movements.position_note: Industrial policy and tariffs - collective and conservative.
movements.where: The Rust Belt: Ohio, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Indiana, Illinois
movements.aaron_note: This would be a new nation to unify these areas in one area and they would adopt a name later. They aren't trying to become a nation so much as an economic area, and if they leave to become a nation they would pick one then.

movements.name: California Republic
movements.where: California entire
movements.aaron_note: This would also include Cascadia.

movements.name: Cascadian Separatists
movements.where: The wet side of the mountains: the Willamette and Puget lowlands, and the northern California coast
movements.aaron_note: This one might be a little tricky because Cascadia separates from California but this movement would want to join with Washington and Oregon and the movement would grow in those states to join them.

movements.name: Central States Union
movements.position_note: Aaron: "Republican but support unions... including libertarian later would help solve some of this." The third axis is what he was missing.
movements.where: The Ohio and Mississippi valleys: Kentucky and West Virginia entire, plus the river counties
movements.aaron_note: This might be something where they would be Republican but support unions. I think that including libertarian later would help solve some of this.

movements.name: Christian Nationalism
movements.position_note: The movement and the position now share a name, which politics ruling 40 makes legal.
movements.where: Southern counties over 100,000 people
movements.aaron_note: This would grow in the south and be different from the Northern Christian Kingdom.

movements.name: Deseret
movements.position_note: Aaron's own: "law of consecration lite... closest analogue is Distributist."
movements.where: The Mormon Corridor across seven states, plus the rest of Utah
movements.aaron_note: In this game they are going to implement a law of consecration lite (which to me the closest analogue would be Distributist, which is a Catholic teaching, so not 100% but kind of close).

movements.name: El Paso United
movements.position_note: His markup.
movements.where: El Paso and the Texas far west
movements.aaron_note: This is one that starts as one of the five Texas contenders and has the ability to become a Free Texas or Rio Grande.

movements.name: Franklin
movements.position_note: Mountain home rule is libertarian-conservative; Anarcho-Capitalism is the alternative.
movements.where: The southern Appalachians: east Tennessee, the western Carolinas, the Virginia coalfields, eastern Kentucky, southern West Virginia
movements.aaron_note: This one should be a movement that grows slowly or comes in later in the game.

movements.name: Front Range Republic
movements.where: Colorado's urban corridor: Denver, Boulder, Colorado Springs
movements.aaron_note: This one I am moving to expansion because of their geography and central location - they have the ability to get a lot of money from trade going through them. Also they have NORAD and air force bases.

movements.name: Great Lakes Free Trade
movements.position_note: A free-trade bloc is market-progressive, and that corner is Digital Technocracy - which fits a trade compact badly.
movements.where: The lakeshore, from Minnesota to upstate New York
movements.goal: a free-trade bloc; a water compact
movements.aaron_note: I like this and I think that the State of Superior or Rochester & Buffalo would be two rivals trying to make this happen.

movements.name: Greater Idaho
movements.where: Rural eastern Oregon
movements.aaron_note: Great as is. I like the idea of this and the other movements in the area competing.

movements.name: Hawaiian Sovereignty
movements.position_note: Sovereignty and land restoration.
movements.where: Hawaii
movements.aaron_note: I moved them to expansionist only because as an island nation I could see them being both vulnerable for resources, but also because they have Pearl Harbor that could be an interesting bonus to their military.

movements.name: Native American Confederation
movements.position_note: The same pair of demands.
movements.where: Tribal-majority and reservation counties across the interior West and Plains
movements.aaron_note: This is great. I think it could be something where the indigenous states would have increased diplomacy and work together for this?

movements.name: New Absaroka
movements.where: Northern Wyoming, southern Montana and the western Dakotas
movements.aaron_note: Looks good and this might be a good one to include in the remaining counties in the area and it would be an autonomous zone.

movements.name: New Confederacy
movements.position_note: States' rights and independence; Fascism is the live alternative, and Aaron has already said this movement's name bothers him.
movements.where: The eleven Confederate states, Virginia to Texas
movements.aaron_note: I wonder if there is a different name for this. If I am being honest this is the one that is most likely to happen if this happened because the confederacy is still strong as an ideology but also feel like it would have a different name than just New Confederacy.

movements.name: New England Revivalist
movements.position_note: "Town-meeting sovereignty" is the most libertarian phrase in the roster - Liberal Anarchy is a real candidate.
movements.where: Vermont, northern New Hampshire, Maine and the Massachusetts hills

movements.name: New England United
movements.position_note: THE ONE HE ASKED ABOUT. Its stated goal is social democracy, which names the position. His Boston question is answerable without changing the movement: the three-axis board carries Distributism as its own position, so Boston's Catholic pull belongs in the minority mix of those counties, not in the movement's placement.
movements.where: The six New England states
movements.aaron_note: Boston is known for its large Catholic population (which is where Distributism comes from) so maybe in Boston they lean Dis/Dem/Social Dem?

movements.name: Northern Christian Kingdom
movements.position_note: Religious government.
movements.where: The interior Northwest: Montana, Idaho, eastern Oregon and Washington, Wyoming
movements.aaron_note: This is a movement that should only grow in rural areas and I am realising that it might be good to create a classification system (later) on what constitutes rural, suburban, and urban.

movements.name: Rio Grande Union
movements.position_note: His markup.
movements.where: The New Mexico corridor from Las Cruces to Taos
movements.aaron_note: This should grow all along the Rio Grande river and as the movement grows El Paso should have an option to either suppress their rebellion and conquer them or to join them as the leader of their cause but in doing so they lose the ability to reunify as Texas, essentially leaving Texas behind for this.

movements.name: Sagebrush Rebellion
movements.position_note: THE ONE THE NEW BOARD WAS BUILT FOR. Aaron: "we might need to add another political alignment with Libertarianism." Market, conservative, libertarian - "return the federal land, county supremacy" lands exactly on that corner.
movements.where: Federal-land counties: Nevada entire, the Colorado high country, the Arizona strip, the Utah desert, western New Mexico
movements.goal: return the federal land; county supremacy
movements.aaron_note: I am seeing that we might need to add another political alignment with Libertarianism. We can keep politics in this table for now but when we get to the politics section we can rework it.

movements.name: Sonoran Republic
movements.position_note: Water rights.
movements.where: The Arizona borderlands
movements.aaron_note: I think this could be a realised state at the beginning of whatever is left of Arizona and New Mexico?

movements.name: State of Jefferson
movements.position_note: The classic rural-libertarian movement; Anarcho-Capitalism is the alternative, and it pairs with Sagebrush.
movements.where: Far northern California and southern Oregon
movements.aaron_note: This will be an interesting one that is fighting against the Greater Idaho movement and possibly working together with them. The thought with these movements and politics is that unlike current American politics there are going to be coalitions so they might be somewhat aligned on politics and 100% aligned with separating but once done there will be more chaos.

movements.name: The Farmers Union
movements.position_note: Price supports and rural credit - already orange in the data.
movements.where: Small-population counties across the Plains and Midwest
movements.aaron_note: No saved markup - this row carries the register's proposal. Its verb was ruled separately by Aaron on 11 September: the Farmers Union is a movement and its verb is Unify (politics ruling 15).

movements.name: Anarcho-Capitalist
movements.where: The Montana interior

movements.name: Delmarva Republic
movements.where: The Delmarva peninsula, southern Maryland and the South Jersey shore

movements.name: Eastern Progressives
movements.where: East Coast metros over 500,000, plus the Hudson valley

movements.name: Fifty-First State
movements.where: The Colorado plains east of Denver
movements.goal: statehood; an end to Denver's rules

movements.name: Libertarians
movements.where: The Great Plains: Oklahoma, Kansas, Nebraska, the Dakotas

movements.name: Techno-Autocrat
movements.where: Silicon Valley, San Francisco, Austin, Seattle, Cambridge, Salt Lake
